findings.issue: The core record moves the nine per-modality file groups (demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes, imaging, waveform telemetry, waveform EEG) and the holdout test set into `resources`, which is declared as sub-resources/component datasets, while the full record places the same nine modality groups in `file_collections` and the holdout set in `subsets`. This is an internal inconsistency in referent modelling between the paired records: the same entities are typed as file collections plus a data split in one record and as component datasets in the other.

Every DistributionFormat object is populated only via `notes`, with no `access_urls`. The declared content (OMOP tables, OHNLP tokens, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst) is format information placed in a free-text catch-all rather than in a declared field of the class; the DistributionFormat class declares only `access_urls` and `notes`, so the format naming has no declared home and duplicates `file_collections[].conforms_to`. Same defect in the core record.
Identical to the full record: all five DistributionFormat entries carry content only in `notes` with no `access_urls`, restating conforms_to values already recorded on the resources entries.

The single DistributionDate object populates only `notes` and leaves `release_dates` empty, and its content is a dataset-size narrative (50,000 admissions released; 45,000 as of August 2025; 100,000 anticipated) rather than distribution dates. The bundle supplies no explicit release date, so the slot is populated with information that answers a neighbouring field (dataset size/status) instead of the field asked for. Same in the core record.
Same as full: `release_dates` unpopulated and `notes` carries admission-count and anticipated-size narrative rather than any distribution or release date supported by the bundle.

The Instance entry for patient admissions sets `counts: 50000` as a single asserted value while the record's own `notes` acknowledge the bundle's two conflicting figures (50,000 from chorus4ai.org; over 45,000 as of August 2025 from the September 2025 webinar). Asserting one figure in the structured field silently selects between disagreeing sources; the disagreement is only recoverable from prose. Same in the core record.

The radiology Instance sets `counts: 7642` (admissions with radiology data, from the website) while its own `notes` record the webinar's statement that 1,000 images were available with de-identification in process. These are different units (admissions vs images) drawn from different sources; conflating them under one Instance obscures which quantity the count denotes.

The single RawData object duplicates content already carried by `raw_data_sources` (local retention of full-text notes, tokens only in enclave) and adds no distinct raw-source facts. It restates a handling policy rather than describing an unprocessed source, and overlaps `is_deidentified.deidentification_details` and `missing_data_documentation`. Same in the core record.

Both Subpopulation objects leave `distribution` empty despite the bundle supporting no distribution figures; more materially, the second entry's `identification` describes contextual data elements (social determinants, distance to nearest hospital) as a basis for identifying demographic subpopulations, which the bundle does not state — the bundle says data elements feature such contextual factors, not that demographic subpopulations are identifiable through them. Inference beyond the source.

`bias_type: selection_bias` is an enum value the schema defines, but the bundle nowhere characterises a bias type. The bundle states only that patient-focused efforts will determine ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias. Assigning a specific bias category and asserting it as a known bias of the dataset is an inference the evidence does not support; the mitigation text is supported but is attached to an unsupported classification. Same in the core record.

`reviewing_organization: 'CHoRUS Ethics pillar (Ethical and Trustworthy AI), CHoRUS consortium'` presents an internal project pillar as a reviewing organization. The bundle describes Ethics as one of three project pillars performing focus groups and legal/ethical research; it does not describe any IRB, ethics committee, or institutional review of this dataset. The slot description asks for IRB approvals, ethics committee reviews, and compliance certifications, none of which the bundle evidences for CHoRUS itself (IRB drafting appears only as a training curriculum topic).

All six Creator objects use `principal_investigator` to hold a person name, including the five CHoRUS leadership-team members whom the bundle does not identify as principal investigators. Only Eric S. Rosenthal is designated PI (NIH RePORTER). Bihorac, Jiang, Strekalova, Rashidi, and Kwong are listed under 'Bridge2AI CHoRUS Leadership Team' in the webinar slide with no role stated. Populating a PI-designating field for them asserts a role the bundle does not support. Same in the core record.
Same as full: five leadership-team members are placed in `principal_investigator` although the bundle designates only Eric S. Rosenthal as principal investigator.

`credit_roles` for Eric S. Rosenthal lists conceptualization, supervision, project_administration, and funding_acquisition. The bundle states only that he is the principal investigator on the award; no CRediT-style role assignment appears in any source. These four enum selections are inferred from the PI title rather than evidenced. Same in the core record.

`publisher` has range uriorcurie and is set to https://chorus4ai.org/, the same value as `page`. The bundle names no publisher for the dataset; the website URL is being reused as an organizational identifier. Same in the core record.

`id` is https://chorus4ai.org/dataset, a URI that does not appear in the bundle (the site's dataset page is referenced only as a nav label 'Dataset'). The synthetic identifier is also the base for eleven fragment identifiers in file_collections and subsets. Constructed rather than sourced, though defensible as a local identifier.

`was_directly_observed: true` conflicts in sense with `direct_collection[0].is_direct: false` in the same record. The bundle supports that clinical data were observed/recorded during care but not collected directly from individuals for this dataset; as populated, the two boolean fields read as contradictory without the qualifying prose. In the core record the DirectCollection object is absent entirely and its content folded into acquisition_methods notes, so the qualification is weaker still.

The core record has no `direct_collection` slot value and instead appends 'Data were not collected directly from individuals for this dataset' to the acquisition_methods notes, alongside `was_directly_observed: true`. Content is displaced from the field that declares it into a catch-all, and the resulting object asserts direct observation and non-direct collection in adjacent fields.

Two VariableMetadata objects are emitted with only `variable_name` and `notes` populated; both names ('Geographic distance to the nearest hospital', 'Social determinants of health') are descriptive phrases from the abstract rather than dataset fields, columns, or variables. The bundle names no variables. The class's declared fields (data_type, unit, categories, measurement_technique) are all empty, so the objects carry no variable structure. Omitted from the core record, which is the safer treatment — an inconsistency between the pair.

The single LabelingStrategy sets `data_annotation_platform: 'CHoRUS visualization and annotation environment'`, a name not used in the bundle. The bundle refers to 'A visualization and annotation environment' being developed; the record converts a descriptive phrase into a named platform. Also, the annotation environment is described as forthcoming, so populating a labeling strategy asserts applied methodology the bundle presents as planned. Same in the core record.

The Splits object populates only `split_details` with the holdout-set description, duplicating `subsets[0].description` verbatim in substance. The bundle documents no train/validation/test partition, only a sequestered holdout; two slots carrying the same single fact. The core record drops `splits` and keeps only the resources entry, an inconsistency between the pair.

The ThirdPartySharing object carries the full registration, licensing-agreement, .edu-email, and access-contact detail in `notes`, which duplicates `license_and_use_terms.license_terms` and `license_and_use_terms.notes`. In the core record this slot is absent and the same content is merged into license_and_use_terms.notes — the pair distributes identical evidence across different slots.

`conforms_to: 'OMOP Common Data Model (OHDSI)'` asserts a single schema for the dataset as a whole, but the bundle documents five distinct standards across modalities (OMOP, OHNLP, DICOM, WFDB/PhysioNet, EDF+/Persyst). The dataset-level value overstates uniformity; the per-collection conforms_to values in file_collections contradict it for four of nine collections. Same in the core record.

A single ExternalResource object bundles four distinct external resources (project website, GitHub organization, bridge2ai.org/chorus page, NIH RePORTER record) into one entry, with all repository, language, and follower detail compressed into one `notes` blob. The slot is multivalued and each resource is a distinct entity; collapsing them populates the slot without representing what it declares. Same in the core record.

`confidentiality_details` restates the same facts carried by `is_deidentified.deidentification_details`, `sensitive_elements[0].sensitivity_details`, and `file_collections[].notes` (controlled access, notes local/tokens only, imaging de-id in process). Heavy duplication across four slots of a single evidence set; no distinct confidentiality claim is added. Same in the core record.

`identifiable_elements_present` and `identifiers_removed` are left empty although the bundle supports statements about them (full-text notes withheld, tokenization applied, DICOM de-identification). Declared fields of the class are unpopulated while the content sits in the free-text `method` and `deidentification_details` fields.

The third Maintainer object ('Maintainers and versions of CHoRUS software packages are tracked on the CHoRUS package status page') records where maintainer information lives rather than naming a maintainer. It is a pointer to documentation, not an answer to the field. Same in the core record.

`status` is a multi-sentence narrative combining release state, access model, anticipated size, and modality progress. The slot expects a status term (draft, published, deprecated). Content that belongs to updates/distribution is packed into a status field. Same in the core record.

The three DatasetLimitation objects leave `recommended_mitigation` empty on two of three and, for the coverage limitation, populate it with 'Consult the modality tables ... and track ongoing releases', which is a navigational instruction rather than a mitigation. Minor: the field is answered with a pointer.
Omitted. The bundle supplies no recommended citation, so omission is correct; noted only to confirm the omission is evidence-consistent and not a gap.

Omitted from both records. The bundle does not state IRB approval or human-subjects determination for CHoRUS itself (IRB appears only as a training-curriculum topic), so omission is defensible; flagged because a reader may expect this slot for a patient-derived clinical dataset and the absence is a deliberate evidence-boundary decision that the reconciliation report should record.

The full record's `subsets` entry (holdout test set, is_data_split: true) has no counterpart typed as a subset in the core record; it appears as a plain resources entry with the `is_data_split` flag dropped. Information present in the full record is lost rather than mapped in the pair.

summary: Both records are broadly faithful to the CHoRUS bundle and stay within the evidence boundary on the major factual claims (award OT2OD032701, 14 contributing hospitals of 20 centers, nine modalities with their standards, 50,000/45,000/100,000 admission figures, controlled access with signed licensing agreement, MIT-licensed tooling). No fabricated dataset facts were found. The defects cluster in four areas. (1) Role over-assertion in creators: five leadership-team members are typed as principal_investigator and four CRediT roles are assigned to Rosenthal, neither supported by the bundle. (2) Structured-field displacement: DistributionFormat, DistributionDate, RawData, ExternalResource, and one Maintainer carry their content in free-text `notes` while declared fields (access_urls, release_dates) stay empty, and external_resources collapses four distinct resources into one object. (3) Source-conflict handling: the 50,000 vs 45,000 admission discrepancy and the 7,642-admissions vs 1,000-images figures are resolved silently in structured `counts` fields with the disagreement recoverable only from prose. (4) Full/core divergence: the nine modality groups move from file_collections to resources, `subsets`+`is_data_split`, `splits`, `direct_collection`, `third_party_sharing`, and `variables` are present in the full record but dropped or merged in the core, so the pair models the same referent inconsistently. Two inferences exceed the source: `known_biases.bias_type: selection_bias` (the bundle mentions managing bias, never a bias type) and the second subpopulation's identification claim. `ethical_reviews` presents an internal project pillar as a reviewing organization where the bundle evidences no IRB or ethics-committee review. Recommended Phase 4 actions: demote non-PI creators out of principal_investigator, attach conflicting counts to distinct source-qualified Instance objects or drop the structured count in favour of notes, split external_resources into four objects, remove or requalify known_biases.bias_type and ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization, drop distribution_dates and the redundant raw_sources entry, and align the file_collections/resources/subsets modelling across the pair.
